The BnF authority heading still reads (18..-19..) and has not been revised.

sources.fullCitation: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique. “René Nazelles.” Musée SACEM, Les créateurs. Author and composer, born in Paris on 8 October 1888, died on 11 September 1975; elected full member of SACEM on 13 September 1911; Prix Salabert, 1958.
sources.title: René Nazelles — Musée SACEM creator record
sources.researchNote: The register settles the life dates that the BnF heading still gives as an open span, agreeing with the years recorded by the film and record databases, and dates his standing in the society from 1911.

media.title: Albert Chantrier and René Nazelles — La Rampe, 1921
media.altText: Black-and-white press photograph of two men in hats and overcoats standing at a café table, reading a sheet of paper.
media.publicCaption: Albert Chantrier and René Nazelles, composer and lyricist of Le Fruit défendu, photographed for La Rampe on the operetta’s run at the Théâtre Cluny. Nazelles went on to write French lyrics for Kaper.
media.publicCreditLine: Unsigned photograph, La Rampe, 9 January 1921, p. 12; Bibliothèque nationale de France, Gallica, ark:/12148/bpt6k55821649.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The photograph appeared unsigned in a French periodical published on 9 January 1921 and is therefore an anonymous work, free in France seventy years after publication, that is from 1992. It was already in the public domain in its source country on the URAA date of 1 January 1996, so no United States copyright was restored, and a work published in 1921 is in any case out of copyright in the United States. Reproduced from the Bibliothèque nationale de France digitisation.
